claims.statement: The dcode Makefile provides network-restricted parallel unit tests and an explicit `update-snapshots` target that runs smoke snapshots with the `--update-snapshots` option.

dcode's unit target runs pytest in parallel with non-Unix sockets disabled, Unix sockets allowed, benchmarks disabled, and coverage; its separate integration target runs with a 30-second timeout, while lint also checks the command catalog and process working-directory policy.

`COMMANDS.md` is an auto-generated reference derived from the slash-command registry; the Makefile has separate regeneration and verification targets, and the catalog distinguishes public commands from hidden commands intentionally omitted from autocomplete and help.

The monorepo treats packages as independently versioned development units with their own `pyproject.toml`, Makefile, and README; developers work inside the changed package and use its Makefile targets.

Both dcode and SDK Makefiles run unit tests in parallel with sockets disabled except Unix sockets, benchmarks disabled, and coverage; their integration targets are separate parallel runs with a 30-second timeout.

Repository guidance requires deterministic, network-free unit tests under `tests/unit_tests/`, reserves networked behavior for `tests/integration_tests/`, uses automatic asyncio mode, and treats unaccepted pytest warnings as failures.

Remote-client tests preserve top-level tracing config, adapt workspace and ownership data at the HTTP boundary, keep primary stream/state results when side accounting fails, and recover one state-write conflict by interrupting active runs before retrying.

Synchronous and asynchronous parallel subagent tests require forked and isolated children not to inherit or overwrite a parent rubric, while both child results and reducer-managed shared completions reach the parent.

Async subagent tests distinguish `fork` from isolated launches: forks transmit a snapshot of retained parent messages plus the task description without message artifacts, isolated launches transmit only the task description, and launch construction must not mutate parent state.

Async subagent fork tests require offloaded media to be rehydrated into the child request, then re-offloaded under the child backend, without retaining `_blob_payloads` in parent or child checkpoint state.
Blob-offload tests require command message updates to be offloaded, reject tampered or malformed blob references as missing-blob text, and preserve inline media if upload fails.

dcode startup tests require resumed history hydration to be idempotent across repeated server-ready events, keep the resuming state until history restoration completes, order restored history before startup output, and block initial submission when resumed-model adoption fails.

dcode modal-command tests drive `ChatInput.Submitted` through the real Textual message pump so Escape remains responsive, reject a second goal while its preference modal is open, and keep queued work blocked until that modal continuation starts.

Headless dcode tests require quiet mode to emit only agent text to stdout, distinguish buffered `stream=False` output from incremental stream output, and forward sandbox type, snapshot name, profile overrides, and filesystem tool allowlists to server startup.

Server-side dcode skill-pinning tests require an outside symlinked skill to obtain persisted trust before pinning, store a stable pinned-skill message snapshot across later edits, clear request-only pin state, recover after a failed pin, and rescan cached skill metadata after a server-process change without losing history.

Sandbox-factory tests require setup failures to delete only newly owned sandboxes, preserve the original setup exception if cleanup also fails, provide install guidance for missing optional provider dependencies, and reject unsupported or reattached snapshot configurations before provider creation.

Dependency-floor automation tests require compatible version selection to respect upper and compatible-release bounds, literal-only manifest rewriting that preserves extras and markers, transitive stale-lock discovery, and failure for unknown or unraiseable narrowed dependency requests.

Dependency-floor workflow tests validate GitHub Actions expression function names, synchronize dispatch package options with release labels, and preserve main ancestry when refreshing an existing automated dependency-bump branch.

ACP execute approval tests require reusable approval to be keyed by the exact serializable command arguments and session context, scoped to one session, and cleared when that session is forgotten; malformed or missing-context calls cannot receive always-allow approval.

ACP local-context middleware keeps initial detected context in the system prompt, then records each summarization cutoff and appends an escaped untrusted internal snapshot only when the detected context fingerprint changes, including recording a failed refresh to avoid retries.

Filesystem permission tests distinguish first-match access policy from recursive-delete policy: exact leaf deletion can use the first matching rule, while a deletion with descendants is blocked without mutation by any overlapping write-deny pattern.

Filesystem interrupt predicates treat bulk operations conservatively: pathless and current-directory searches can intersect protected paths, and `glob` checks an absolute or escaping pattern independently of its nominal path to prevent HITL bypass.

Filesystem backend tests enforce virtual-root containment and media safety: traversal is rejected, ripgrep results through symlinks escaping the root are filtered, and oversized video files are rejected before their bytes are read.

dcode model allowlist parsing accepts ordered, deduplicated exact provider:model entries and provider wildcards, while rejecting malformed or bare Bedrock entries so a declared policy cannot silently become unmatched.

Talon media tests require outbound markdown media under a supplied root to resolve to a supported regular image or video within that root after symlink resolution, rejecting absolute, traversal, home, URL, and escaping paths.

Talon sandbox startup is fail closed and its composite backend routes only assistant skills, memory, and blob namespaces to host filesystems while execution and other files use the sandbox; cancellation during asynchronous startup still closes the owned sandbox.
Talon stores inbound image payloads as SHA-256 blobs in the assistant artifacts directory rather than checkpoint message state, and rehydrates the image in the model request.
